deep.reconstruction:
Context (my reading of folios 38v–40r): this is part of Gauss's lattice-point evaluation of the biquadratic character, i.e. a Gauss-lemma analogue in the Gaussian integers. The page conventions appear to be m = a+bi and M = A+𝔅i, both odd. Points x+yi run over the half-system square 0<x,y<1/2, with ξ+ηi = m(x+yi) and X+Yi = M(x+yi) along a line of constant η. Θ(z) is an index in {0,1,2,3}, a power of i, so everything is read mod 4. On the previous page (Art.12) Gauss wrote, for fixed η: Σ±Θ(fM/m) = k°Θ(X°+Y°i) − k°°Θ(X°°+Y°°i) + Σk. There k=0 if [ξ] is even and k=±1 if [ξ] is odd, for each interior crossing where X or Y is an integer.

This page first fixes the sign of k at an odd crossing. Define α = sign of Re(M/m) and 𝔟 = sign of Im(M/m).
(a) If X is an integer, test four conditions: η even; X even; [Y] even; M/m in quadrant 2 or 3 (α<0). Then k=+1 if 0, 2 or 4 of them fail, and k=−1 if 1 or 3 fail. In modern form (mine): k = (−1)^(η + X + [Y] + [α>0]).
(b) If Y is an integer, the conditions are: η even; Y even; [X] even; M/m in quadrant 1 or 2 (𝔟>0). Again k=+1 when all, two or none hold, so k = (−1)^(η + Y + [X] + [𝔟<0]).

Worked example (continuing the previous page), using floor values:
- [ξ°] = [−161/22] = −8, even, so k°=0.
- [ξ°°] = [−12/11] = −2, even, so k°°=0.
- [ξ''] = [−57/18] = −4, even, so k''=0.
- [ξ'] = [−83/19] = −5, odd, so k'=±1; Gauss finds k'=−1.
Hence the sum is −1 (written ΣΘ(fM/m) = −1).

Art.13 treats the degenerate case where an endpoint ξ° or ξ°° of the η-line is itself an integer. This happens only at the lattice points x=1/2, y=0 (where ξ+ηi = m/2 and η = b/2) or at the origin (where η=0). Four cases follow by the quadrant of m:
- I. m in quadrant 1, at x=1/2, y=0: η = b/2 is an integer and Y°° = 𝔅/2 is an integer. Use Θ(A/2 + (𝔅/2)i) if 𝔟<0, but Θ(A/2 + (𝔅/2 − 1)i) if 𝔟>0. This is a tie-break: the boundary point is pushed infinitesimally.
- II. m in quadrant 2, at the origin (x=y=η=0): X°°=Y°°=0. By convention Θ(0) = 2,3,0,1 and k°° = 1,0,0,1 as M/m lies in quadrant 1,2,3,4.
- III. m in quadrant 3, at x=1/2, y=0: X°+Y°i = A/2 + (𝔅/2)i. Replace it by Θ(A/2 + (𝔅/2 − 1)i) when 𝔟<0.
- IV. m in quadrant 4, at η=0: Θ(X°+Y°i) = 0,1,2,3 and k° = 0,1,1,0 by quadrant of M/m.

These conventions feed directly into the 'Decident' rule of the next page (Art.14). There the correction terms are:
- m in quadrant 2: 2,0,0,3, which is −k°°Θ°° = −2,0,0,−1 mod 4.
- m in quadrant 4: 0,1,2,0, which is k°Θ° = 0·0, 1·1, 1·2, 0·3.
Both agree with this page.
errors: 'k''=−0' should simply be k''=0; it is consistent with [ξ''] = [−57/18] = −4 being even.

The value k'=−1 cannot be fully checked from the data given: η is not recorded. Also Y' is ambiguous between previous-page values (3/19 vs 33/19 gives [Y'] = 0 vs 1). With X'=−1 odd and α>0 (M/m in quadrant 4), the sign depends on η and [Y'].

Minor, on the next page: the condition '½(A−1) ungerade' for cases I/III would by this page's setup more naturally be [ξ°°] = [a/2] = (a−1)/2 odd, so a and A may be confused there. Not an error on this page itself.

The tie-breaking rules of cases I–IV are stated without justification; they are conventions equivalent to an infinitesimal displacement of the boundary point. They appear consistent mod 4 with the later summary.

results.what: Parity rule for the ±1 contribution k at a lattice crossing (X or Y integer): k = (−1)^(η + X + [Y] + [Re(M/m)>0]), resp. (−1)^(η + Y + [X] + [Im(M/m)<0])
results.modern_name: Sign bookkeeping in a Gauss-lemma / Eisenstein-type lattice point count for the biquadratic residue character
results.usually_credited_to: Eisenstein (1844) for published lattice-point and Gauss-lemma style proofs of biquadratic reciprocity; Gauss for the 1832 statement

results.what: Boundary/degenerate-case conventions (Art.13) for when an endpoint of the η-line is a lattice point (origin or m/2), with Θ(0) assigned by the quadrant of M/m
results.modern_name: Boundary corrections in counting lattice points of a half-system for Z[i]
results.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; technical detail of lattice-point proofs (Eisenstein, later Gauss-lemma treatments)

results.what: Numerical example: computing the decident sum = −1 for a specific m, M
results.modern_name: Worked example of the biquadratic character computation

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss is well known to have possessed a proof of biquadratic reciprocity that he never published. Fragments in his Nachlass (Werke II/VIII) contain related material. A detailed Gauss-lemma lattice-point bookkeeping in Z[i], resembling Eisenstein's later approach, is a notable unpublished technical detail. It is not a new theorem, and its existence in some form is not unexpected.

checkable.asserts: Parities of [ξ°], [ξ°°], [ξ'], [ξ''] in the example: even, even, odd, even. So k°=k°°=k''=0 and only k' is nonzero.
Case II conventions give the next page's correction 2,0,0,3 as −k°°Θ°° mod 4.
Case IV conventions give the next page's correction 0,1,2,0 as k°Θ° mod 4.
At x=1/2, y=0 one has η = b/2 (and similarly Y = 𝔅/2 for M), the degenerate point of cases I and III.
Compact form of the first k-rule: k=+1 iff an even number of the four conditions fail.

transcription_corrections: 'Σ Θ λM/m = −k' should likely read 'Σ ±Θ(fM/m) = −1'; the final symbol looks like −1, and 'f' matches the previous page's notation.
In Art.13 the clause after 'a und A' is uncertain; it seems to read 'a und A ungerade voraussetzen', with an interlinear 'oder X°, Y°, X°°, Y°°'.
Case II: the image reads 'X°° = 0, Y°° = 0' after the cancelled 'Dafür ist Y'.
The column heading for the k values in case II appears as 'und k°°' at the right.
